anchorData: VIDEO CLIP (Nairobi-Nakuru highway near Naivasha, straight level road, dry, daylight). Positive direction = towards Nakuru. Car A = blue Toyota Axio being overtaken. Car B = white Subaru overtaking. Lorry L = oncoming lorry heading towards Naivasha (negative direction). Each car is 5 m long. Time t = 0 s is the instant B starts to accelerate. KEY NUMBERS: At t=0 both cars show 72 km/h (20 m/s) and B's front bumper is 20 m behind A's rear bumper. Car A keeps a steady 20 m/s (72 km/h) throughout. Car B accelerates uniformly from 20 m/s to 30 m/s (108 km/h) in 5 s, so a = (30-20)/5 = 2 m/s^2, then holds 30 m/s until it is back in lane. Overtaking is complete at t = 7.5 s, when B's rear bumper is 20 m ahead of A's front bumper. Lorry L travels at a steady 20 m/s (72 km/h) towards the cars, velocity -20 m/s, and at t=0 its front is 500 m ahead of B's front. SPLIT-TIME TABLE (distances travelled from the start point at t=0, in metres). t(s) | v of B (m/s) | B distance | A distance | B minus A (extra distance B has gained): 0 | 20 | 0 | 0 | 0; 1 | 22 | 21 | 20 | 1; 2 | 24 | 44 | 40 | 4; 3 | 26 | 69 | 60 | 9; 4 | 28 | 96 | 80 | 16; 5 | 30 | 125 | 100 | 25; 6 | 30 | 155 | 120 | 35; 7 | 30 | 185 | 140 | 45; 7.5 | 30 | 200 | 150 | 50. Car A velocity is 20 m/s at every time. Milestones: at t=5 s B's front is level with A's front (B has gained 25 m = 20 m gap + 5 m length of A); at t=5.5 s B's rear passes A's front (gained 30 m); at t=7.5 s B has gained 50 m = 20 m start gap + 5 m (A length) + 5 m (B length) + 20 m finishing gap, so overtaking is complete. Totals: B travels 200 m, A travels 150 m, L travels 20 x 7.5 = 150 m. B and L together cover 200 + 150 = 350 m, so when B pulls in the lorry is 500 - 350 = 150 m away, and with closing speed 30 + 20 = 50 m/s they would meet 150/50 = 3.0 s later (safety margin). RELATIVE SPEEDS: B relative to A = 30 - 20 = 10 m/s = 36 km/h after t=5 s (it grows from 0 at t=0 to 10 m/s at t=5 s; at t=0 both are 20 m/s so relative speed is 0). B and L closing speed = 30 + 20 = 50 m/s = 180 km/h. B-minus-A gap is the area under B's relative velocity graph: 1/2 x 5 x 10 = 25 m, then 10 x 2.5 = 25 m, total 50 m. AREA UNDER B's v-t GRAPH: trapezium 0-5 s = (20+30)/2 x 5 = 125 m; rectangle 5-7.5 s = 30 x 2.5 = 75 m; total 200 m. WHAT-IF for lesson 9 only: if the lorry were 400 m away at t=0 instead of 500 m, margin = 400 - 350 = 50 m, closing 50 m/s gives 1.0 s, which is unsafe. SUPPORTING SITUATIONS (use only in the lessons named in lessonMap). (1) Boda boda trip, Naivasha town: rider leaves the stage, goes 3 km east to the market in 10 min (0.3 km/min = 18 km/h), then turns back west 1 km to the school, taking 5 min more. Total time 15 min; distance = 4 km; displacement = 2 km east of the stage; average speed = 4 km / (15/60 h) = 16 km/h. (2) Matatu journey Nairobi to Naivasha: road distance 90 km in 1.5 h, average speed 60 km/h. (3) Parked matatu at a stage 5 km from Naivasha town: displacement stays 5 km for 30 min, velocity 0. (4) Returning cyclist (Naivasha to Lake Naivasha gate and back): 0-30 min goes 6 km away (0.2 km/min = 12 km/h); 30-40 min rests at 6 km; 40-60 min returns home (-0.3 km/min = -18 km/h). Total distance 12 km, final displacement 0, average speed 12 km/h, average velocity 0. Displacement-time points (min,km): (0,0),(30,6),(40,6),(60,0). (5) Steady car on graph: 60 km/h so (0,0),(30,30),(60,60) in (min,km). (6) Meeting problem Naivasha-Nakuru, 60 km apart: a matatu leaves Naivasha for Nakuru at 60 km/h and a private car leaves Nakuru for Naivasha at 90 km/h at the same moment. They meet after 60/150 = 0.4 h = 24 min, 24 km from Naivasha (matatu 60 x 0.4 = 24 km, car 90 x 0.4 = 36 km, 24 + 36 = 60). (7) Braking matatu (velocity-time lesson 6 and 7): speed at the start 20 m/s, then table t(s) 0,2,4,6,8,10 and v(m/s) 20,16,12,8,4,0; deceleration = 2 m/s^2 (acceleration -2 m/s^2); stopping distance = 1/2 x 20 x 10 = 100 m. (8) Steady-speed section for velocity-time graphs: Car A, 20 m/s for 0-7.5 s, distance 150 m.
characters: Car A: blue Toyota Axio driven steadily by Mr Kamau at 20 m/s (72 km/h), the car being overtaken. Car B: white Subaru driven by Wanjiru, the overtaking car. Lorry L: oncoming lorry driven by Mr Otieno from Nakuru towards Naivasha at 20 m/s, 500 m ahead of B at t=0. Setting: Nairobi-Nakuru highway near Naivasha, straight dry road, daylight. Learner characters (optional): Achieng, who watches the speedometers from the back seat of Car B, and Kiprono, who films from the roadside. Boda boda rider Juma: trip from Naivasha stage to the market and back to the school (see anchorData). Cyclist Atieno: cycles from home to Lake Naivasha gate and back. Matatu 'Naivasha Express': Nairobi to Naivasha, 90 km, 1.5 h; also the matatu leaving Naivasha for Nakuru at 60 km/h and the one braking from 20 m/s. Private car from Nakuru at 90 km/h. All lessons may rely only on facts in anchorData.
outcome: Wanjiru in Car B speeds up from 20 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s (acceleration 2 m/s^2), draws level with Car A at t=5 s, and pulls back into lane at t=7.5 s after travelling 200 m while Car A travels 150 m. Both speedometers look high (72 km/h and up to 108 km/h) but Car A looks slow from B because relative speed is only 10 m/s (36 km/h) in the same direction, starting from 0 when the acceleration begins, whereas the oncoming lorry closes at 50 m/s (180 km/h). The manoeuvre is safe because B needs 350 m of road shared with the lorry and the lorry started 500 m away, leaving 150 m, or 3.0 s, to spare; a lorry only 400 m away would leave just 1.0 s, which is unsafe.
conventions: Positive direction is towards Nakuru; the oncoming lorry has negative velocity -20 m/s. Time symbol t (s); initial velocity u, final velocity v (m/s); acceleration a = (v - u)/t, in m/s^2; deceleration is negative acceleration, written as a magnitude with the word 'deceleration' (e.g. deceleration 2 m/s^2 means a = -2 m/s^2). Distance is total path length, a scalar, in m or km. Displacement is straight-line change in position with direction, a vector, in m or km. Speed = distance / time (scalar). Average speed = total distance / total time. Velocity = displacement / time (vector, direction by sign). Convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6, and m/s to km/h by multiplying by 3.6 (72 km/h = 20 m/s). Graph conventions: displacement-time graph has t on the x-axis and displacement on the y-axis, gradient = velocity; velocity-time graph has t on the x-axis and v on the y-axis, gradient = acceleration, area under the graph = displacement (distance when velocity does not change sign). Relative speed: same direction = difference of speeds; opposite directions = sum of speeds; always state the viewpoint (e.g. 'B relative to A'). Always say 'overtaking car B', 'overtaken car A' and 'oncoming lorry L'. Treat cars as points moving in a straight line except when lengths (5 m each) and gaps (20 m) are used for the complete overtaking distance. Use these exact numbers; do not invent other values for the phenomenon. Use 'speed up', 'slow down' in everyday language and 'acceleration', 'deceleration' formally. Use the word 'gradient' for slope. Graph scales: 1 cm = 1 s on the x-axis for lessons using m/s data.

lessonMap.focus: Phenomenon: Overtaking on the Naivasha highway
lessonMap.teaches: Observing the overtaking clip, predicting how long and how far the overtake takes, and noticing what is puzzling (both speedometers high yet A looks slow from B); generating questions for the Driving Question Board. No formulas taught.
lessonMap.usesData: Qualitative clip description only: A at 72 km/h, B at 72 km/h at the start then faster, oncoming lorry, B returns to lane. No split-time table or computed values shown.

lessonMap.focus: Distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration
lessonMap.teaches: Defining and distinguishing distance vs displacement and speed vs velocity, with acceleration as rate of change of velocity (qualitative, with units); no calculation of acceleration.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: DQB questions about 'how far' and 'how fast'.
lessonMap.usesData: Boda boda trip (4 km distance, 2 km displacement), matatu Nairobi-Naivasha (90 km, 1.5 h), cyclist Atieno (12 km distance, displacement 0), and which of A, B, L has constant velocity and which accelerates.

lessonMap.teaches: Using velocity = displacement/time and a = (v - u)/t with unit conversion km/h to m/s, including negative sign for deceleration and opposite direction.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: definitions of velocity and acceleration.
lessonMap.usesData: Car A 150 m in 7.5 s gives 20 m/s; B accelerates 20 to 30 m/s in 5 s gives a = 2 m/s^2; lorry -20 m/s; 72 km/h = 20 m/s, 108 km/h = 30 m/s; boda boda 18 km/h on first leg; braking matatu a = -2 m/s^2.

lessonMap.teaches: Choosing scales, plotting points and drawing straight-line displacement-time graphs for stationary, steady-speed and returning movements; no interpretation beyond describing the shape.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 2-3: displacement and velocity as displacement/time.
lessonMap.usesData: Parked matatu 5 km (horizontal line), steady car 60 km/h points (0,0),(30,30),(60,60), returning cyclist points (0,0),(30,6),(40,6),(60,0) in (min,km).

lessonMap.teaches: Reading velocity as gradient (sign shows direction), identifying rest as a flat line, and finding the meeting point as the intersection of two graphs.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: drawn graphs; Lesson 3: velocity calculation.
lessonMap.usesData: Cyclist graph gradients 12 km/h, 0, -18 km/h; meeting problem Naivasha-Nakuru (matatu 60 km/h and car 90 km/h meet at 24 min, 24 km from Naivasha).

lessonMap.teaches: Plotting velocity-time graphs from data tables and recognising the shapes for speeding up (rising line), steady speed (horizontal line) and slowing down (falling line).
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: graph-plotting skills; Lesson 3: acceleration values.
lessonMap.usesData: Car B table t=0 to 7.5 s with v 20 to 30 m/s, Car A constant 20 m/s line, braking matatu table t 0-10 s with v 20 to 0 m/s.

lessonMap.teaches: Finding acceleration or deceleration from the gradient and distance travelled from the area under the graph (trapezium, rectangle, triangle).
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 6: velocity-time graphs; Lesson 5: gradient as a rate.
lessonMap.usesData: B gradient 2 m/s^2; area 125 + 75 = 200 m for B and 150 m for A; braking matatu gradient -2 m/s^2, stopping distance 100 m; check against the split-time table.

lessonMap.teaches: Relative speed of two bodies: subtract speeds for the same direction, add speeds for opposite directions, stated from a stated viewpoint, explaining why A looks slow from B.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 3 and 7: velocities of A, B and L; B-minus-A gaining distance.
lessonMap.usesData: B relative to A grows from 0 to 10 m/s (36 km/h); B and L closing speed 50 m/s (180 km/h); the B-minus-A column of the table (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 35, 45, 50 m) and the 50 m gained.

lessonMap.teaches: Combining time, distance and relative speed to decide whether an overtake is safe, using the total road needed (350 m) and the safety margin in metres and seconds.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 3, 7 and 8: acceleration, areas, relative speed.
lessonMap.usesData: Overtake time 7.5 s, 50 m relative distance, B 200 m and lorry 150 m, lorry 500 m away leaves 150 m (3.0 s); what-if lorry 400 m away leaves 50 m (1.0 s), unsafe.

lessonMap.focus: Final model and answer to the driving question
lessonMap.teaches: Synthesis only: presenting a complete model (annotated graphs plus calculations) of the overtake and answering the driving question and the two KICD questions; no new skill.
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-9: all graphs, calculations and DQB questions.
lessonMap.usesData: Whole anchorData: split-time table, outcome (200 m vs 150 m, 7.5 s, 2 m/s^2, 10 m/s relative, 150 m / 3.0 s margin).
